description: Team's major objective is to build a health monitoring devices (yes hardware) to track and monitoring blood and health of the astronauts. Our team is looking for hardware experts (or not its fine), ML, Computer Vision.
summary:
Astro Health Monitor is software that lets a crew look after its own health when Earth is too far away to help. On the way to Mars a message can take up to 22 minutes each way, so astronauts must detect problems and act on their own.

We developed an Android app and Windows software that read heart rate, blood oxygen and beat-to-beat timing from spacesuit sensors or onboard medical devices over Bluetooth or USB. In our prototype, a fingertip pulse oximeter stands in for those sensors. Everything runs offline. The software compares each astronaut with their own baseline, flags a stress response from heart-rate variability, then guides resonance breathing and checks the recovery: a closed loop, not just a monitor. An explainable guide adds symptom checks, a reaction test, skin and height scans, and nutrition targets from NASA’s exploration requirements (JSC-67378), organized around NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight.

It matters because early detection and guidance on board protect crew health and mission success, and the same tool can serve remote and isolated teams on Earth.
